newsitem.title: SENEGAL: France Telecom buys Senegal SONATEL stake.
newsitem.headline: France Telecom buys Senegal SONATEL stake.

text.p: Senegal on Monday sold a one-third stake in state telecommunications Company SONATEL to France Cables Radio, a subsidiary of France Telecom, for 650 million French francs, officials said.

France Cables Radio, which is a 100-percent-owned subsidiary of France Telecom, took a 33.33 percent plus one share in SONATEL under an agreement signed in Dakar by Senegal's Minister of Economy amd Finance, Papa Ousmane Sacko, and France Cables Radio President Michel Hirsch.
The state intends to keep a stake of around a third, while 10 percent of the shares will go to SONATEL staff and five percent to an African partner that has not yet been chosen, officials said.
The remaining shares could be sold to other institutions and the public.
"We are honoured and happy to have won this competition in a fair manner," Hirsch said at the signing ceremony.

France Telecom started talks for the purchase of a one-third stake in SONATEL after the cancellation on April 16 by Senegal of a provisional deal worth 70 billion CFA francs ($116 million) with a consortium led by Swedish company Telia Overseas TELI.CN.
The Swedish consortium wanted a seven-year concession which would have lasted only until the proposed end of SONATEL'S monopoly over the fixed-line network.
France Cables Radio, which has agreed a 20-year concession, plans to expand Senegal's telephone line network to 285,000 lines by 2001 from 100,000 now.
"We have decided to privatise SONATEL because we have regional and continental ambitions," Sacko said.
Senegal also plans to liberalise its cellular telephone sector next year, with January as the target date for the start of a second network.
SONATEL started the West African nation's first cellular telephone service in October, using a GSM system. ($ = 606 CFA francs) ($ = 6.06 French francs)
